quote: Theorem 1. Let X1, . . . , Xn (X1*, . . . , Xn*) be independent and non-negative random variables with Xi ∼ r(x; αi, βi) (Xi* ∼ r(x; αi*, βi)), i = 1, . . . , n. Further, suppose that Ip1, . . . , Ipn (Ip*1, . . . , Ip*n) is a set of independent Bernoulli random variables, independent of the Xi's (Xi*'s), with E[Ipi] = pi (E[Ip*i] = p*i), i = 1, . . . , n. Assume that the following conditions hold: (i) r(x; α, β) is increasing [decreasing] and convex in α for any β and any x > 0; (ii) ∂r(x;α,β)/∂α is decreasing (increasing) in β for any α and any x > 0. Then, for (α, β) ∈ Sn− (Sn+) and (α*, β) ∈ Sn− (Sn+), we have Π_{i=1}^n p*i ≤ Π_{i=1}^n pi and (α1, . . . , αn) ≼w [≼^w] (α1*, . . . , αn*) ⇒ Y1:n* ≤hr Y1:n.
model: other: smallest claim amount Y1:n of a portfolio of risks Yi = Ipi Xi (Bernoulli occurrence indicators times independent heterogeneous severities); equivalent to series-system minimum
family: general model: severities specified only through hazard rate function r(x; α, β) with two parameters
compared: occurrence-probability vectors p vs p* (via product comparison) and severity parameter vectors α vs α* (weak majorization); common β vector

The proof text confirms α sorted decreasing (α1 >= ... >= αn) under Sn− with β increasing. The α* vector is defined with a possibly different symbol αi* but shares the same βi.

quote: Example 1. Let Xαi ∼ Burr(αi, βi, 2) (Xα*i ∼ Burr(αi*, βi, 2)), for i = 1, 2, 3. Further, suppose that Ip1, Ip2, Ip3 (Ip*1, Ip*2, Ip*3) is a set of independent Bernoulli random variables, independent of the Xαi's (Xα*i's), with E[Ipi] = pi (E[Ip*i] = p*i), for i = 1, 2, 3. We take (α1, α2, α3) = (4, 0.7, 0.2), (α1*, α2*, α3*) = (4.2, 0.6, 0.3), (β1, β2, β3) = (5, 3.5, 1.2), (p1, p2, p3) = (0.2, 0.3, 0.4), and (p*1, p*2, p*3) = (0.25, 0.35, 0.25). It is clear that the conditions of Theorem 5 are satisfied. So, we have Y1:n* ≤hr Y1:n. Figure 1 represents the function rY1:n*(x) − rY1:n(x), which agrees with the intended result.
